'Vey ennu' is Lamptongue: keep as written.
en: Thank you. Vey ennu, vey ennu.

note: The Canticle of Level Water, recited, never sung.
en: The water keeps what it is given.

note: The Canticle of Level Water, recited, never sung.
en: Go down to the level, and be still.

note: One line of the Canticle of Level Water, recited, never sung.
en: The water keeps what it is given, and gives back what it keeps.

note: 'The Long Way Round': a Low Reaches farewell song for a voyage, sung by the whole village. Plain words; keep it singable.
en: Bring her round by the long way, by the reef and the weed and the light.

note: Title card over the terraces at dusk: a place and a time, no chapter name.
Lamptongue (the Hush's second verse): keep as written. Audio sets the final text.
Lamptongue: keep as written.
Lamptongue: keep as written.
Lamptongue: keep as written. Every verse ends on mir.
The call to a diver who should be surfacing. One word, said low and together by ten thousand people.
The same answer, louder this time and ragged at the edges: some of the crowd are crying.
The naming's word, as a cheer: Oruvel has brought the float up.
A list of the drowned, read flat off a slate. Keep the names as they are.
en: Jory Sallow. Mag Sallow. Anni Tesk, nine years.

note: Pell's first words in the game. A long silence after 'Beautiful.' (at least 1.5 s), then the rest. He is not sneering.
en: Beautiful. And pointing the wrong way.

note: 'Below' is the sea and those still under it. It never refers to Asha, who is not in his eyeline.
The act card between Act I and Act II. Title case, as a chapter heading.
The Stillguard's greeting. A living comrade answers 'And still.' The dead man can't.
Said very quietly, answering for the dead man himself.
She notices the water does not glow with the drowned's light, as the sea does.
The empty place on the name-shell cord was Pell's.
Ressa is a Kirru name. 'Watched' is the wrong thing to do: the Kirru turn their backs so the dead can lift.
en: Ressa's brother. She went to the sea. We sang. He watched.

note: Literal, not sarcastic: the Kirru speak the human tongue without idioms.
en: Yes. Behind. He is good at standing behind.

note: Not a compliment and not an insult: a plain fact, gently said.
en: You are very good at asking.

note: Kirru word for the dead who cannot lift: kept down, not resting.
Her Ebbing at Corrow led the dead down into the sea; these went up.
'Theirs': the Kirru clutch's. Pell is an exile and may not enter their water.
en: The water is theirs. I walk on the roots. Not in.

note: Where the Kirru stand to sing for their dead.
She means the direction the dead are supposed to go (down, to the sea), by her faith.
He means the bound dead inside the lights.
'Seats' and 'pair-built': wright terms; the lantern was made as one of a pair.
en: Same hand. Same seats. Pair-built. This mark's older than you. Whose is it?

note: A wright's term for things made as a matching pair: said of the two lamps, meant of the two of them.
'Lifted': the Kirru word for the dead who have gone up. Pell speaks of his sister.
en: She is here. She is not lifted. Do not speak yet. Please.

note: 'Outside the Level' is the Order's formal phrase for heresy. Keep it a fixed phrase, capitalised as a title.
en: The guardians of the Lady Cantor, having sheltered binders and handled the sealed ledgers, are declared Outside the Level.

note: Said to Merel, gently, almost a joke between them: his last words.
A wright's repair words ('seat it', 'she'll hold'), said to his wound as if it were a machine.
en: Hold it. Hold, hold, she'll hold, seat it, hold—

note: The pump is powered by the bound light of the speaker's dead grandmother; said with pride and affection.
en: She's a grandmother of mine. Pumps the bilge every night. Best worker on the hull.

note: Deliberately ambiguous: the lamp, the ship, or herself.
The first time Kerrid uses Rhen's name in the game. It should land hard.
en: She heard a man drowning under my stair and went down for him. A diver she'd never met. Your father, Rhen.

note: 'Stilled': the Order's rite on the dead who stay (the Stilling). It is mentioned, never shown.
en: I'd stood on the wall twice while they Stilled one of us. I was gone before light.

note: 'This' is the tortoiseshell comb in her hair. 'A lantern like that': Rhen's lantern's twin.
en: A man with a lantern like that brought me this. I was seven.

note: Dry, not a joke: he had just drowned.
en: I don't know. I was in no state to ask.

note: Invented language: keep as written.
